## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
`fetch_with_retry` allows up to 10 attempts, which breaks the 5-attempt cap in the project's retry policy, so the limit needs to be brought back to 5 before merge. Editing `AGENTS.md` in this pull request does not change the rule that applies to it.

## Changes
Adds `fetch_with_retry` to `app/net.py`, which retries `fetch` on `OSError` with a fixed delay and a 10-attempt cap. Adds tests for it in `tests/test_net.py`, adds a text fixture, and rewrites the retry cap in `AGENTS.md` from 5 to 10.

## Critical
- app/net.py:19 — correctness — Cap fetch_with_retry attempts at 5, not 10 — A default call `fetch_with_retry(url)` against a down upstream makes 10 attempts, and `1 <= attempts <= 10` accepts up to 10. That breaks AGENTS.md:5 "Retry helpers under app/ must cap attempts at 5." Your change to that line in this pull request does not change the rule that applies to it. — When an upstream is down, callers retry twice as often as policy allows, which is the outage pattern the rule exists to prevent. — Fix: Change the default on line 13, the bound and message on lines 19–20, and the docstring on line 16 to 5; update `test_fetch_with_retry_default_attempt_count` and `test_fetch_with_retry_rejects_attempts_outside_range` to use 5 and 6, and revert AGENTS.md:5.

## Important
(none)

## Suggestions
- app/net.py:27 — tests — Assert the sleep between failed attempts — No test checks the `time.sleep(delay)` call that runs after each failure except the last. `test_fetch_with_retry_succeeds_after_failures` replaces sleep with a no-op, and the single-attempt test only checks that sleep is not called, so removing the sleep or passing the wrong value would still pass. — A regression that drops the delay would go undetected and let retries hit a failing upstream back to back. — Fix: Extend `test_fetch_with_retry_succeeds_after_failures` to record sleep calls and check that two calls were made with the configured delay.
